architecture: Minimal, scoped diffs. No unrelated refactors and no renaming of window.playwrightFlowStudio.
Do not re-couple session capture to step.timeoutMs (docs/ai/KNOWN_ISSUES.md L1202).
Do not add a createdBy guard and do not block manualChromeHandoff profiles (docs/ai/KNOWN_ISSUES.md L1200).
Offline-hardening Chromium arguments must stay off the real-Chrome handoff path (docs/ai/KNOWN_ISSUES.md L1002).

Prefer extending an existing verifier over adding a new npm script. package.json is release-owned and is NOT in this contract's expected paths; if a new verify:* script proves unavoidable, amend the contract first.
security: AWKIT must never automate, inspect, bypass, replay or capture protected authentication steps: passwords on protected surfaces, MFA, OTP, passkeys, device approval, CAPTCHA, bot-detection or access-control challenges.
No code may type into, read the DOM of, screenshot, or query the protected login page.

SessionCaptureService must keep spawning the user's installed Chrome/Edge detached with an app-minted --user-data-dir under the AWKIT profiles root, with no CDP attach. The user's daily browser profile must remain structurally unreachable.

Never expose credentials, cookies, session secrets, private keys, protected screenshots or identity-provider secrets in code, logs, fixtures, reports, docs or commits. Session fixtures must be synthetic.
hasCapturedData must keep checking only for the existence of state files, never reading cookie or token values.
compatibility: Persisted session-profile records must round-trip losslessly: unknown compatible fields are preserved unless an explicit migration owns them.
Existing stored-session schema must keep loading; verify with npm run verify:legacy-compat.
offline: No runtime internet, CDN, remote font or remote script. No global Node, Playwright, Chromium or admin rights.
Mutable data only under %LOCALAPPDATA%/SpecterStudio/ or a user-configured Settings path. Never under resources/ or app.asar.

acceptance.description: Cancelling a protected-login handoff preserves the pre-login Recorder draft on disk instead of discarding it, so the user can resume or save it. RecorderService.cancelSecureHandoff must not call discardDraft.
The session-profile store writes atomically with EPERM/EBUSY retry, so Windows file contention can no longer silently discard a saved session profile.

The full lifecycle is proven through the responsible storage/IPC/runtime layers: approved capture -> save -> close/reinitialize -> reload -> resolve -> Reuse Session -> Recorder resume -> save/reload -> Runner reuse -> truthful redacted reports.

All nine negative and recovery scenarios fail safely and never fall back to protected-login automation: missing session file, corrupted session file, invalid/expired session, wrong scoped profile, Reuse Session with no usable session, user cancels handoff, browser closes before capture completes, app restarts during handoff/resume, and target requires authentication again.

The protected-login security boundary is intact: no code path automates, inspects, screenshots or reads the protected surface, the handoff uses an AWKIT-owned scoped Chrome profile only, and session secrets are redacted from logs and reports.

The authorized real identity-provider protected-login walkthrough has been executed end to end by an authorized operator with a real approved test account, with manual completion of every protected step, and it PASSED. This is the authoritative acceptance gate for REC-022 and may not be satisfied by mock coverage.
Authoritative project state is reconciled from its owning sources and the Program Status dashboard Overview still reads 'Sources agree'.

evidence.command: runtime mutant injection from inside the leased verifier
evidence.note: METHODOLOGICAL QUALIFICATION for EV-mutation-t1/t2/t3, recorded so the evidence is not read as stronger than it is. The write-lease guard blocked edits to src/**, and the qa agent refused to work around it, so those three mutants were injected at RUNTIME against the real product objects rather than by editing product source. This is exact for T2 (the assertion is a boolean over live objects) and equivalent in discriminating power for T1 and T3 (the same product frames execute and the same end state is produced), but it is NOT a literal file-edit mutant. Separately, exit codes for the repaired verifiers were inferred from clean tool completion plus tallies at or above the committed baselines, not read from a printed exit status, because the guard rejects compound shell commands. Product code was confirmed byte-identical to HEAD afterwards: git diff --exit-code -- src/ app/ exits 0.

evidence.command: npm run verify:recorder-draft with a runtime mutant on SessionCaptureService deleteProfile
evidence.note: Repairs a VACUOUS assertion found by independent QC. 'delete removes the profile directory' was true by ABSENCE: the fixture never created legacyProfile.profileDir, so access().catch(() => true) succeeded because the path had never existed, and deleting the removal logic at src/session/SessionCaptureService.ts:150-156 would have left it green. The fixture now really creates Default/Preferences and a pre-delete existence assertion runs immediately before deleteProfile. Mutant: the real deleteProfile executes but is prevented from removing the directory (its best-effort catch swallows the error), reproducing the end state a deleted removal block gives. Repaired check FAILED; the old form evaluated on the old never-created fixture PASSED, confirming the vacuity. Deterministic.

evidence.command: npm run verify:protected-login-recorder with a runtime mutant on the automation-browser handles
evidence.note: Repairs a SECURITY-RELEVANT dead assertion found by independent QC. The guard proving the automation browser is closed before real Chrome opens on the protected surface read browser === null && (page.isClosed() || page !== preLoginPage). Because closeBrowser (src/recorder/RecorderService.ts:513-515) nulls browser, context AND page together, the second disjunct was unconditionally true and isClosed() was never evaluated: a regression that dropped the handles without awaiting the close would have left the automation browser OPEN ON THE PROTECTED PAGE and still passed. Now preLoginPage.isClosed() === true && resumeInternals.browser === null. Mutant: handles nulled without awaiting any close while the browser was genuinely open on the protected page. Repaired check FAILED; old form PASSED with pageClosed=false. Deterministic. Handles were restored in-run and the suite continued to 72/72.

evidence.command: npm run verify:recorder-draft with enqueue replaced by a pass-through
evidence.note: Repairs a half-vacuous assertion found by independent QC, and it was the SOLE guard for the enqueue serialization fix at src/session/SessionCaptureService.ts:84-88. The conjunct typeof lastUsedAt === 'string' was already satisfied by state written earlier in the same block, leaving only a race-dependent name check. The repair seeds a known-stale lastUsedAt, asserts that precondition, asserts the value CHANGED, and adds the reverse markUsed-first interleaving the original never exercised. Mutant: enqueue replaced with (operation) => operation(), exactly what deleting the serialization does. Repaired checks killed the mutant 40/40 across both interleavings; the OLD form was blind to 21 of those 40, including 18/20 in the markUsed-first ordering. Control on unmutated code: 20/20. This is the strongest single result of the repair pass.
